industry.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'Why the Defence Industry de-rated from July to October 2026 while Theon's forecasts rose' and on the condition written on this row last week, which fired: a third reading at F with no demand read in the strategist sources. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the Researcher's report finds multiples cut while estimates held, the industry's premium over the STOXX 600 down from 60% to 12% (Bernstein, 9-Oct-26), exit multiples moving towards 13 times operating profit as the order boom gives way to execution (Jefferies, 28-Oct-26, 'Defense Likely at Peak Fundamentals vs. Aero'), and budgets converting slowly into contracts (German run-rate, Boxer approvals); the UK Budget funded the existing Defence Investment Plan but postponed the 3%-of-output decision to the 2027 Spending Review. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: F now, D prior; both sectors F. A government-contracted revenue line with a falling multiple is a Fragility case in this regime, not a defensive one. The sector rows split the view: Primes D (land and ammunition hit hardest), Non-primes C (electronics and optronics held up). One live holding, Theon (4.05%), judged in components 4 and 5; no Pool name sits here, so the Lists are unmoved. Counter-case: estimates have not fallen, the premium compression may already be the exit multiple, and German approvals may convert (Rheinmetall 5-Nov-26, Bundestag budget vote 27-Nov-26). Back to C if relative strength leaves F as approvals convert; to F on a signed Ukraine settlement followed by defence fund outflows.

sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'Why the Defence Industry de-rated from July to October 2026 while Theon's forecasts rose': the short-cycle land and ammunition names that sit in this sector were hit hardest by the de-rating (Bernstein, 29-Sep-26), exit multiples are moving towards 13 times operating profit, and the conversion of German budgets into contracts lags the headlines. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: F now, C prior, the third reading at F. Counter-case: the large, proven, government-contracted cases are what a risk-off market is meant to pay for, and Rheinmetall's print on 5-Nov-26 and the Bundestag vote on 27-Nov-26 are dated chances for conversion to show. Back to C when relative strength leaves F with approvals converting.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
